title: A sport of 11 alternating rounds, 4 minutes of chess and 2 of boxing, came from a comic book
hook: There's a sport where you play chess, then switch to boxing and trade punches

open.title: A sport where boxers trade punches, then sit down at a chessboard
open.line: Two fighters alternate between a chessboard and a boxing ring.

summary: Chessboxing came from a 1992 Enki Bilal comic. Dutch artist Iepe Rubingh made it real and became the first world champion in 2003.

text: Two fighters alternate between a chessboard and a boxing ring.
Chess, then boxing, then chess again.
The 2005 rules: 4 minutes of chess, 2 of boxing.
They alternate like this for 11 rounds.

panels.text: Wait, you play chess right after getting punched?

text: Dutch artist Iepe Rubingh invented it.
He said you need the fitness to calm your pulse for chess.
Checkmate or knockout wins. Run out of chess time, you lose.
Chess draw? Boxing points decide. Still tied? Black wins.
Actually, this sport came from a comic book.
A 1992 Enki Bilal comic, set on a ravaged planet in 2096.
In the comic, they box a full fight, then play chess.
Rubingh found that impractical and made them alternate.

panels.text: So he just turned a comic into real life.

text: At the first world title fight in 2003, Rubingh himself fought.
In round 11, his opponent ran out of chess time. Rubingh was the first champion.

sources: The Guardian (2005-10-31): Introducing the world's most unlikely sport: chessboxing
